questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of underground railways in London
Feeling awkward and the unspoken social rules behind it
How to make polite conversation with strangers at work
Why teenagers hate watching TV with their parents
questions.why: Neil says they're looking at awkwardness and how it is connected to social rules.

questions.q: When did Dan use to feel awkward?
options: Waiting at the bus stop in the morning
On the crowded underground to work
When talking about money with friends
Watching love scenes on TV with his parents
questions.why: He remembers feeling awkward watching explicit love scenes with his parents.

questions.q: Which example do the presenters give of breaking a social rule?
options: Asking a stranger at a bus stop how much they earn
Talking about the weather with a neighbour
Sitting far away from other people on a bus
Watching romantic films on TV with family
questions.why: Dan says it would be awkward to ask a stranger how much money they earned.

questions.q: How does Dr Raj Persaud describe social rules?
options: Written down but rarely followed
Different in every family
Almost invisible, yet very powerful
Easy to see with a brain scanner
questions.why: He says they're 'almost invisible - yet we all obey them' and are 'massively powerful'.

questions.q: What problem does Dr Persaud raise about studying social rules?
options: People refuse to talk about them with researchers
You can't see them with a brain scanner or microscope
They change every year, so studies go out of date
They are too simple and obvious to be worth studying
questions.why: He says you couldn't use an MRI brain scanner or a microscope to find them.

questions.q: How did 'breaching experiments' discover social rules?
options: By asking people to write down the rules they follow
By reading old books about manners and etiquette
By secretly watching people in their own homes
By breaking a rule on purpose and watching reactions
questions.why: Dr Persaud says, 'You breached the social rule on purpose.'

questions.q: What happened in the train experiment?
options: Someone sat right next to the only passenger in a carriage
Someone talked very loudly on the phone for the whole trip
Someone walked through the train asking passengers for money
Someone stood in the doorway so nobody could get off
questions.why: He describes sitting next to the only person in a carriage.

questions.q: How did researchers know they had found a rule?
options: The passenger started a friendly conversation
The passenger complained to the train staff
The passenger seemed uneasy, and even got off
The passenger ignored them and fell asleep
questions.why: If it led to discomfort and the person got off immediately, a rule was discovered.
